faq: Tokens that track a listed share 1:1, traded on crypto exchanges with USDT. The main families are xStocks (OKX, Bybit, Kraken, Gate), rToken (Bitget), bStocks (Binance) and Ondo tokens (MEXC). OKX and Bitget describe them as economic exposure to the share, without direct share registration or voting rights.
What is the difference between a stock token and a stock perpetual?

A stock token is bought and held like spot crypto. A stock perpetual is a USDT-margined contract with no expiry that lets you go long or short with leverage: up to 100x on Bitget, up to 20x on Kraken. A perpetual gives no shares.
Can I trade US stocks on the weekend?
Yes, on many venues. OKX xStocks trade 24/7. The stock perpetuals of Bitget, OKX, Binance and Bybit trade 24/7. Bitget rToken trade 24/5, with 90 major names open 24/7 since August 2026.

It depends on the token. Bitget rToken credits net cash dividends in USDT after a default 30% withholding. OKX xStocks and Binance bStocks reinvest the net dividend into the token balance instead of paying cash.
Can US residents buy tokenized stocks?
No. Bitget rToken, OKX tokenized stocks, Binance bStocks and Kraken xStocks all exclude the United States and US persons.
Contracts on private companies before they list, such as OpenAI and Anthropic on OKX and Bybit or JIO on Bitget (up to 20x). They give no shares, no IPO allocation and no shareholder rights.
Bitget stock perpetuals charge 0.02% maker and 0.06% taker. Bybit xStocks spot charges 0.2%. Kraken charges no trading fee when you buy xStocks with USD or USDG.
